standard.title: Area of Triangles and Parallelograms
standard.description: solve problems involving the area of triangles and parallelograms using established formulas and appropriate units
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can establish and apply the area formula for a rectangle (from AC9M6M02). Students understand area as the measure of a 2D region and can use appropriate units.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve problems involving the area of triangles and parallelograms using established formulas with appropriate units.

nodes.label: Deriving the triangle area formula
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students understand why the area of a triangle is half the area of a related rectangle or parallelogram, and can state the formula A = ½bh.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain using a diagram why A = ½bh for a triangle, connecting to the rectangle formula.
nodes.typical_width: Derive the formula using multiple triangle types (right-angled, acute, obtuse) and verify the connection to the enclosing rectangle in each case.
wider: Investigate using dynamic geometry software: slide the apex of a triangle at a fixed altitude and observe that the area is constant — explain why.
Explore how the formula applies when the height is outside the triangle (obtuse case).

response_modes.reason: Students who derive the formula only for right-angled triangles often believe the formula changes for acute or obtuse triangles. Multiple triangle types resolve this.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who believe the formula only applies to right-angled triangles misidentify the height in Node 2 problems — applying A = ½bh with the slant side instead of the perpendicular height produces systematically wrong answers for all non-right-angled triangles.
success_criteria: States the area formula for a triangle and explains its derivation.
Correctly identifies the base and corresponding perpendicular height.
Does not confuse the slant side with the perpendicular height.

nodes.label: Applying area formulas to triangles and parallelograms
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students calculate the area of triangles and parallelograms using established formulas, selecting appropriate units.
nodes.minimum_width: Calculate the area of a given triangle and a given parallelogram using their formulas.
nodes.typical_width: Solve problems involving composite shapes (decompose into triangles and rectangles); select appropriate units; convert between units if needed.
wider: Solve practical problems: floor plans, sail areas, land parcels — requiring decomposition into triangles and parallelograms.
Investigate First Nations design elements that use triangular and parallelogram forms — calculate areas in context.

response_modes.reason: Area formula application errors are common in non-standard orientations and composite shapes. Varied practical contexts with different orientations are necessary.

success_criteria: Correctly calculates the area of a triangle using A = ½bh.
Correctly calculates the area of a parallelogram.
Uses appropriate units and converts if necessary.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Practical area problems involving decomposition of composite shapes (floor plans, land parcels) offer advancing students rich multi-step spatial reasoning within the Year 7 band.
